game: Timberborn 1.1.2.4; maps read with the app's importer and validated with its validators on our canonical settle

method.sizeClasses: small ≤ 12k tiles, medium ≤ 20k, large ≤ 45k, max above (investigation/analyze_maps.py)
method.unusualShapes: a side over 256 or an aspect of 4 or more: counted, kept out of the size bands
method.water: every number about water comes from our canonical settle of each map's own sources (PLAN §10), never from the water a file stores; wet = depth ≥ 0.1, badwater = contamination ≥ 0.3
method.features10: caves, overhangs, relics, geothermal fields, mine sites, weirs, plugs and thorns are compared within the 1.0+ maps only
method.generated: seeds 1–30 of every built theme at 128², Normal, default settings, measured with the same code

flow.note: Main flow from the strength-weighted centre of the clean sources to the depth-weighted centre of the draining map edge; north is +y. 'closed': no water leaves the map; 'local': source and outlet within 10% of the map's side; 'none': no clean source.

popularity.note: Hints, never proof: Spearman rank correlations over workshop maps. 'subscribersForAge' is log lifetime subscribers after a fit on log age; 'withinAuthor' takes each prolific author's (3+ maps) own mean out; 'favouriteRate' is log favourites per lifetime subscriber, and 'favouriteRateWithinAuthor' the same with each prolific author's mean taken out. 'stars' is Steam's 1-5 star rating, where an item has enough votes to show one. ci90 is a bootstrap interval; one that spans 0 is noise.

reservoirs.note: The validator's own dam sampling near the start (straight dams across clean water, crests 1-3, lines up to 21 tiles); 'holding' = its reservoir holds a Normal drought's need of 380 blocks; 'short dam' = 5 tiles or fewer.

analyzeMaps.note: investigation/analyze_maps.py aggregate() over each group, on our canonical settle's water (analyze_py.py)

catalogue.name: Island in a moat
catalogue.description: A central island or plateau ringed by water: a moat, a round lake with an island, or a river that loops round the middle.
catalogue.build: A lake with an island (lake `islands`): the moat-island recipe. A flowing ring river needs a loop the river tool refuses.
catalogue.risks: The island is its own level region: it needs slopes or player stairs; a ring that cuts the start off from its water.

catalogue.name: Spiral mountain or quarry
catalogue.description: A ramp that winds up a central peak, or down into a pit, one level per step; sometimes a channel spirals with it.
catalogue.build: Stacked landforms along a spiral with a pinned slope at every step: the spiral-mountain recipe. Better as a builder (spiral: centre, radius, turns, levels, up or down).
catalogue.risks: Every step needs its slope, or the ramp strands the colony; a peak above 16 levels is out of reach.

catalogue.name: Concentric rings
catalogue.description: Nested rings of terraces or water round a centre, like a target or the Eye of the Sahara.
catalogue.build: Nested landforms with terraced edges, or rings of lakes with islands.
catalogue.risks: Rings of cliffs cut the land into strips no building fits on; each ring needs a way through.

catalogue.name: Crater or caldera lake
catalogue.description: A round basin with a raised rim holding a lake, often with an island in the middle and a notch where it spills out.
catalogue.build: A ring of landforms and a lake inside it, with an island; the lake tool routes its outlet through the wall: the crater-lake recipe.
catalogue.risks: A rim with no outlet overflows at its lowest point; a crater start floods when its lake rises.

catalogue.name: Volcano
catalogue.description: A cone rising above the land with a crater at the top, often spilling badwater down its flank.
catalogue.build: Cone landforms with a badwater basin at the summit, whose outlet runs down the flank: the volcano recipe. Better with a `cone` landform (radial profile).
catalogue.risks: Badwater down the flank must reach the river below the start; a tall cone shades nothing but blocks routes.

catalogue.name: Shaped lake or island
catalogue.description: A lake, island or range drawn as a recognisable shape: a heart, a star, a spiral, a symbol.
catalogue.build: Any outline: lakes and landforms take polygons: the heart-lake recipe.
catalogue.risks: Thin points and narrow necks of a shape become one-tile channels or unreachable tips.

catalogue.name: Real geography
catalogue.description: A real place in miniature: a continent, a lake district, a mountain range.
catalogue.build: Heightmap import (M11) scaled to 0–16, then water and resources placed on it.
catalogue.risks: Real coastlines leave little flat land; the sea at the map edge drains unless sealed.

catalogue.name: Archipelago
catalogue.description: Many islands in a sea or lake, crossed by shallow water or bridges.
catalogue.build: The Islands theme; a lake's `islands`.
catalogue.risks: Small islands without trees or water; a sea above the 0.55 water cap.

catalogue.name: Lone island
catalogue.description: One island in a sea that fills the map to its edges: survival on a single landmass.
catalogue.build: An Islands variant with one island; a sea to the edge needs its edge sealed (sources along it) or it drains.
catalogue.risks: Water share far above today's caps; little land to grow.

catalogue.name: Mesa field
catalogue.description: Many flat-topped columns of different heights standing out of lower ground, some crowned with ruins.
catalogue.build: Cliff-edged landforms, ruin fields on the tops: the mesa-field recipe.
catalogue.risks: Mesa tops need stairs: the payoff must be optional, never the start's needs.

catalogue.name: Tower or sky island
catalogue.description: Very tall, narrow landforms or islands raised high above the floor, sometimes with water on top falling off the edge.
catalogue.build: A tall mesa with a lake on top whose outlet cascades down: the hanging-lake recipe. True floating islands need overhangs (Later).
catalogue.risks: The top is out of reach without stairs; water on top needs a spring and an outlet.

catalogue.name: Cluster of basins
catalogue.description: Many round bowls, some wet and some dry, joined by channels or saddles.
catalogue.build: Lakes and bowl landforms; the Lake Basin theme's planned Crater lakes premise.
catalogue.risks: Dry bowls fill in a flood; each bowl needs an outlet or it holds badwater.

catalogue.name: Ribbon map
catalogue.description: A long thin strip, 3–20 times longer than wide, travelled end to end.
catalogue.build: Non-square sizes (48–256 a side); beyond 256 needs a map-resizer mod.
catalogue.risks: Rivers along a ribbon run along an edge (edges drain); little room for set pieces.

catalogue.name: Great scarp or wall
catalogue.description: One long cliff or wall splitting the map into an upper and a lower world, crossed by a fall or a breach.
catalogue.build: A cliff-edged landform across the map and an on-river fall where the river crosses it.
catalogue.risks: The upper world needs its own slopes or stairs; the river's step must be a planned fall.

catalogue.name: Parallel ridges
catalogue.description: Ridges and valleys running side by side across the map.
catalogue.build: Ridge landforms; the Highlands planner.
catalogue.risks: Each valley is a corridor: reach from the start is short without slopes over the ridges.

catalogue.name: Contour terraces
catalogue.description: Hillsides stepped like rice terraces, following the contours, with water running down between them.
catalogue.build: Terraced edges (bands 6–12 deep); the generator's terraces.
catalogue.risks: Very narrow terraces hold no buildings.

catalogue.name: Big meanders and oxbows
catalogue.description: A river that loops back on itself, leaving oxbow lakes and near-islands.
catalogue.build: Oxbow lakes beside a river: the oxbow-lake recipe. Loops that nearly close need looser river rules.
catalogue.risks: A near-closed loop floods its neck; a start inside a loop is cut off by water (water never blocks walking, but it slows).

catalogue.name: Hairpin canyon
catalogue.description: A river that doubles back in tight switchbacks inside a canyon.
catalogue.build: Needs a switchback river: the river tool refuses hairpin turns.
catalogue.risks: Adjacent reaches at different levels leak into each other unless the wall between them is thick enough.

catalogue.name: River that splits round an island
catalogue.description: A river that divides into two arms round a big island (an eye) or fans out into a delta.
catalogue.build: Braided channels in the Delta planner; a single big split needs a fork builder (a river that divides and rejoins).
catalogue.risks: Unequal arms: one arm dries or takes all the water.

catalogue.name: Hub and spokes
catalogue.description: Channels radiating from a central pool or island like a compass rose, often symmetric.
catalogue.build: Rivers into a central lake (Lake Basin's inflows); spokes flowing out need a lake with several outlets.
catalogue.risks: Outflowing spokes split the flow thin; the hub floods the centre.

catalogue.name: Branching network
catalogue.description: A tree of rivers or dry rifts branching across the map, meeting at a trunk.
catalogue.build: Tributaries (up to 3 today); more branches and dry rifts need a network planner.
catalogue.risks: Many thin streams: each too shallow to pump.

catalogue.name: Perched channel or aqueduct
catalogue.description: Straight water channels raised above the ground on embankments, crossing or bridging, like ruined aqueducts or a highway interchange.
catalogue.build: A causeway landform with a drawn river on top; untested.
catalogue.risks: An embankment one tile thick leaks through its sides unless its banks are raised; the river's bed never rises downstream.

catalogue.name: Landmark falls
catalogue.description: Wide or twin waterfalls meant to be seen, often horseshoe-shaped.
catalogue.build: Standalone waterfalls: the twin-falls recipe.
catalogue.risks: A wide lip needs flow (about 0.4 per tile for an official look); the plunge pool must drain.

catalogue.name: Chain of lakes
catalogue.description: Lakes strung together by short channels and falls, each at its own level.
catalogue.build: Lakes whose outlets run to other lakes (the lake tool).
catalogue.risks: A lake without inflow slowly dries; a chain that settles slowly.

catalogue.name: Flood challenge
catalogue.description: The map starts flooded (or in a badwater sea) and the colony must drain or tame it.
catalogue.build: Needs a challenge validation profile: today start.dry and water.no_flood forbid it.
catalogue.risks: Unwinnable starts; the canonical settle is not what the player sees on day one.

catalogue.name: Buried water
catalogue.description: Old canals and rivers blocked with rubble, or water hidden underground, for the player to open.
catalogue.build: Plugged spillways and Blockage lines (M7); water under roofs is Later.
catalogue.risks: A plug that releases a flood onto the start; hidden water the player never finds.

catalogue.name: Human-made landmark
catalogue.description: Ruins of a megadam, a fortress wall, a stepped pyramid, a highway or a temple, built from terrain and ruin columns.
catalogue.build: Landforms for walls and stepped pyramids, ruin fields shaped as buildings; best as stamps (M11).
catalogue.risks: Walls that cut the map; ruins inside the start's clear zone.

catalogue.name: Choose your side
catalogue.description: Two or more distinct regions to expand into, each with its own trade-off.
catalogue.build: The second district site (M7) and premises with two expansion zones.
catalogue.risks: One side is always better: the choice is fake.

catalogue.name: Carpet forest
catalogue.description: The whole map under dense forest the colony clears as it grows.
catalogue.build: Forest density above today's 200% cap.
catalogue.risks: Trees on every buildable tile slow the first days; a dead carpet on dry soil.

catalogue.name: Caves and tunnels
catalogue.description: Overhangs, tunnels and caverns: a start under a cliff, water running through the mountain.
catalogue.build: Outside today's scope: voxel terrain and water under roofs (Later).
catalogue.risks: Unsupported terrain collapses; water under roofs is not simulated by our model.

catalogue.name: Hazard play
catalogue.description: Unstable cores, badtide drains and timed sources that reshape the map as cycles pass.
catalogue.build: Unstable cores (advanced), badwater settings; timed sources are an Advanced placement.
catalogue.risks: Cores near dams or the start; timed water the checks cannot see.

catalogue.name: Symmetric layout
catalogue.description: Mirror or rotational symmetry: a map that looks designed.
catalogue.build: The symmetry tool (M10).
catalogue.risks: One start: symmetry must not duplicate it.

catalogue.name: Diorama
catalogue.description: A tiny map (64² or smaller) packed with vertical detail.
catalogue.build: Sizes from 48²; smaller needs the game's 4–47 range.
catalogue.risks: Density rules for 96²+ misfire on tiny maps.

variety.method: V(A,B) = 0.5·L/L0 + 0.5·F/F0: L the layout distance under the 8 rotations and mirrors, F the feature distance over 14 size-free numbers; a set's variety is the mean V over its pairs (lib/variety.ts).

withLandmarks.note: V3 = (L/L0 + F/F0 + P/P0) / 3, P the Jaccard distance between pattern sets

premiseMix.note: River Valley's 30 seeds with every recipe's 128² maps mixed in: the theme with its eleven recipes as premises

score.method: lib/score.ts: 11 components, each 0–1; score = 100 × weighted mean. Parameters in investigation/workshop/score-params.json.

criterion.rule: the recommended official maps (Plains, Lakes, Waterfalls) in the top third of the 19 official scores

mesa-field.name: Mesa field with ruins on top

spur-narrows.name: Dam narrows between two hillside spurs

narrows.note: The best dam site within 40 tiles of the start (the validator's), measured where it is
